blocks.text: Separating one or two components from a simple mixture needs simple techniques such as filtration, distillation and solvent extraction, but complex mixtures need more powerful ones. Chromatography is a versatile and important analytical technique that separates the individual components of a complex mixture according to their different affinities for two phases. Complex mixtures, such as the dyes in flowers, pollutants in a water body or medicinal extracts from leaves, can be separated this way. Chromatography is used to identify, purify and measure substances with high precision, which makes it an efficient modern analytical tool in medicine, forensic science and environmental science.

blocks.caption: Figure 28.1: The complex mixture of pigments in leaves can be efficiently separated using chromatography (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 28.1).

blocks.text: Adsorption is a surface effect in which particles collect only on the outer surface of a solid; activated charcoal, for example, adsorbs gases and impurities on its surface, which is why it is used in filters. Of the many types of chromatography, three important ones are paper chromatography (PC), thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and gas chromatography (GC).
